scope: Independent visual review of current baseline screenshots, interaction evidence and owning CSS. Focus on hierarchy, density, responsive composition, feedback and Morzsa identity. No other specialist reports inspected.
strengths: Warm cream/sage surfaces, forest text, restrained terracotta actions and food/mascot artwork remain coherent across onboarding, pantry, list, recipes and cooking. No generic dashboard redesign is warranted.
Onboarding has one prominent next action per card, practical examples and optional shortcuts. Pantry setup shows zero selected items until the user chooses, then offers explicit save.
Shopping rows give the checkbox and ingredient name priority; quantities remain readable while notes, categories and deletion are revealed in the item editor.
Ingredient details present Van otthon, Kevés and Elfogyott in plain text. The recipe ingredients sheet distinguishes unknown available quantity, low stock and an explicit shortage.
Guided cooking prioritizes one instruction and a large fixed next-step button. Completion keeps ratings/notes optional and does not imply automatic pantry consumption.
limitations: External Google Fonts were blocked. Typography observations apply to fallback rendering; serif fallback in some dialogs is not classified as a brand defect.
AI-generated covers were intentionally unavailable. Ingredient illustrations and missing-image states were reviewed; generated-photo quality was not.

The 019-D-recipe-detail capture is visibly clipped and has navigation displaced above the viewport bottom. It was inspected but excluded as support for a product-layout defect pending stable recapture.
Responsive evidence beyond 390x844 has not arrived at this draft checkpoint; review will be expanded before finalization.
Contrast claims use recorded rendered axe results and owning CSS. No screen-reader or physical-device testing was performed.

findings.title: Shopping save feedback covers the next primary action
findings.affectedScreen: Shopping planning and subsequent recipe navigation on mobile
reproductionSteps: At 390x844, add shopping items and open the Tej item editor.
Save 0.5 l so the list shows 500 ml and the save/undo toast appears.
Try Boltban vagyok before the toast expires, or switch to Recipes while it is still visible.
findings.expectedBehavior: Saving feedback and Undo remain visible without covering the next primary action or intercepting its click.
findings.actualBehavior: The fixed save/undo toast overlays the store-mode button and intercepts pointer events. The captured journey timed out after 5 seconds waiting to click it. The same toast continues over recipe contextual controls after navigation; source keeps it for 10 seconds.
findings.userImpact: A successful routine edit temporarily prevents users from entering shopping mode and makes unrelated recipe controls difficult to use.

evidence.description: Save/undo toast visibly covers the shopping dock
Shopping toast persists over the recipe screen
C-journey records exact toast subtree intercepting pointer events

findings.recommendedSolution: Position save/undo feedback above the actual visible dock with reserved space, or inline with edited list content. Preserve Undo accessibility while preventing overlap; reconcile the toast on destination changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Immediately after editing an item, the store-mode action has an unobstructed hit area at every required mobile viewport.
Undo stays accessible by touch and keyboard during its available interval.
Navigating to recipes while feedback is visible does not obscure contextual actions.
regressionTests: Save a fractional shopping quantity; assert elementFromPoint at the store-mode action resolves within that button and click without waiting for toast expiry.
Repeat with a visible toast at 320x640, 375x812 and 390x844; navigate to recipes and verify contextual controls remain unobstructed.

findings.title: Small cooking labels fall below the normal-text contrast threshold
reproductionSteps: Open guided cooking and inspect the small Vezetett főzés label on cream.
Start a timer and complete or resume cooking; inspect its small step label on the sage timer card.
Run contrast checks on rendered elements.
findings.expectedBehavior: Small status and timer labels meet WCAG 2.2 AA normal-text contrast of at least 4.5:1.
findings.actualBehavior: Recorded axe output measures #BF4E2C on #F8F3E9 at 4.37:1 for the 12px cooking label and #667260 on #E8EDDE at 4.25:1 for the 11px timer step label. Both are below 4.5:1.
findings.userImpact: Low-vision users and users glancing at the screen while cooking have less reliable access to small contextual status text.

evidence.description: Small terracotta cooking-status text on cream

findings.recommendedSolution: Use a darker brand-compatible text token for these small labels while retaining cream/sage surfaces and terracotta accents elsewhere. Verify contrast in both states.
acceptanceCriteria: Both rendered small-label foreground/background combinations measure at least 4.5:1.
Axe reports no color-contrast violation for the identified cooking and timer labels.
Visual hierarchy and timer numerals retain their purpose and readability.
regressionTests: Run axe on guided cooking and completion with an active timer.
Capture both states at mobile widths and check computed foreground/background contrast.
